t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup split vertically. Left 58%: a warm limestone sheet with a small mono uppercase eyebrow, a large light-weight sans headline in sentence case, a short mono paragraph and a four-column table with hairline rules and steel-blue mono row numbers for <CONTENT>. Right 42%: a full-height deep navy panel with a duotone macro close-up of a white polypropylene pipe butt-fusion weld running diagonally, shallow depth of field, overlaid with crisp white hairline leader lines, dimension arrows and tiny mono labels. Square corners, calm and precise.
signature_idea: A plain who-does-what table set against a navy panel where a single fusion weld is magnified and annotated like an inspection photo.
strengths: the weld macro shows the actual PP material story and is visually striking
table is legible, numbered and maps directly to a role table component
palette stays navy, limestone and steel blue
light headline and mono details match the brand pairing
weaknesses: the table side is a plain table with no visual idea; the panel is only decoration beside it
annotation labels are garbled and duplicated ('fusion zone' three times, stray digits)
invented regulatory figures in the intro would be mistaken for facts
bold column headers are heavier than the brand type
image and table do not refer to each other
brand_fit_why: On-palette with light headline, mono codes and square corners, and the PP weld is on-offer, but garbled labels and an unrelated plain table reduce precision.
